question.problem: A plane can travel $\frac{3}{5}$ of a mile in $6$ seconds.  What is the unit rate of miles traveled per second?
question.worked_solution:
To compute the unit rate of miles per second, we divide the number of miles, $\frac{3}{5},$ by the number of seconds, $6$, as follows:    

$$
\frac{3}{5}÷6
$$

Dividing a fraction by a whole number is equivalent to multiplying the fraction by the reciprocal of that whole number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5}÷6 & =\frac{3}{5}÷\frac{6}{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\times \frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{3\times 1}{5\times 6} \\  & =\frac{3\times 1}{5\times 2\times 3} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{3}\times 1}{5\times 2\times \cancel{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the unit rate in this situation is $\frac{1}{10}$ miles per second.
